items.title: Pahang Ruler: Not every Orang Asli land claim is 'customary land'
items.summary: ROMPIN: The Sultan of Pahang has called for greater clarity on the use of the term 'customary land' (tanah adat), saying Orang Asli land claims must be assessed according to the legal status of the land. Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah said the Orang Asli community must not be misled into believing that every area they claim as 'customary land' automatically belongs to them. Instead, Act 134 provides for the term 'Orang Asli area' (kawasan Orang Asli) under Section 6 and 'Orang Asli reserve' (Rizab Orang Asli) under Section 7, which may be declared by the state authority through official gazettement.

items.title: Ex-PM Muhyiddin’s trial: PMO gave names of contractors for Jana Wibawa projects, Finance Ministry officer says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) during the Muhyiddin administration had proposed contractors that passed the Finance Ministry’s evaluations and eventually won multi-million ringgit government projects under the Bumiputera contractors’ programme Jana Wibawa, a senior Finance Ministry (MOF) officer told the High Court today. Rosni today said she chaired an MOF committee that evaluated whether contractors were qualified for Jana Wibawa projects. Rosni said her committee had evaluated these contractors for Jana Wibawa projects after receiving their names from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), stressing that the committee would not have evaluated these companies if the PMO did not propose them.

items.title: Three Nepalese workers rescued from burning shoplot
items.summary: Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations John Sagun Francis said firefighters rescued the trio at 7.19am after they became trapped on the second-floor roof and awning. "Firefighters immediately carried out rescue and firefighting operations, and all three victims were successfully brought to safety," he said. The fire, reported at 7.01am along Jalan Pasar, involved two adjoining two-storey shophouses.

items.title: Thai police charge pub owner as Bangkok fire death toll hit 41
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thai police said on Tuesday they submitted charges against the owner of a Bangkok pub to prosecutors, a month after a fire at the venue killed more than 40 people in the country's deadliest blaze in five years. The charges include negligence causing death, negligence causing serious injury to others, negligence causing physical and mental harm to others, negligence causing a fire, and operating an entertainment venue without a license, Police Major General Kiatikul Sonthinern, the district police commander, told Reuters. "The owner, however, was still being treated in hospital and was unable to acknowledge the charges," Kiatikul said.

items.title: Media industry moves to develop unified audience measurement framework
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian media industry is developing a unified Single Audience Measurement (SAM) framework to tackle longstanding issues caused by fragmented audience data. Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF) chairman Datuk Rafiq Razali said the framework aims to provide a single, de-duplicated view of consumers across television, radio, digital media, streaming, social networks and mobile applications, reflecting modern media consumption habits. "The media industry cannot make tomorrow's decisions using a fragmented picture of today's audience.

items.title: Anwar: Tabung Haji probes stretch beyond RCI, enforcement ordered to act fast, firm, fearless
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — Investigations and actions by authorities regarding Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) issues may go beyond the scope and period examined by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI), said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said the RCI is the basis or “parent” for the investigation and scrutiny regarding the issue and there is no obstacle for the authorities to examine matters that occurred before or after the period involved. Earlier, Anwar in his closing speech ordered that follow-up actions regarding the TH issue be implemented firmly and immediately.

items.title: Pakistan top court orders ex-PM Imran Khan be moved to hospital from jail
items.summary: ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court of Pakistan ordered on Tuesday that former Prime Minister Imran Khan be moved to hospital from jail, his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party said, meeting a longstanding demand of his party and family, who had raised concerns about his health. The court has directed Khan be moved to Shifa International Hospital within 48 hours and remain there until September 16, Khan's spokesperson Naeem Haider Panjutha said on X. Since he lost power in a no-confidence vote, Khan has faced multiple cases, including over state gifts and an unlawful marriage.

items.title: Kundasang disaster risk: Fed, state govts must work together, says Kurup
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: The federal and Sabah governments must work together to mitigate impacts that could exacerbate disaster risks in Kundasang. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) Minister Datuk Arthur Joseph Kurup acknowledged that the risks associated with natural causes and climate change in Kundasang had increased over the years. "Under my ministry, we have the Minerals and Geoscience Department, which could monitor all the tectonic activities and slope movements that could give warning to the state.

items.title: Probe into Malaysia Airlines pilot focused on possible organised crime links
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The police probe into the Malaysia Airlines pilot accused of smuggling drugs into Indonesia is focused on determining whether the suspect is linked to organised crime syndicates. He said he received regular updates from Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan, and was inclined to allow the department to complete its probe first. Saifuddin said the pilot, a Malaysian, was arrested by Indonesian authorities and was therefore subject to the republic's laws.

items.title: Budget 2027 to heed rakyat’s voices, PM Anwar says, as energy crisis weighs on households
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Budget 2027 must heed the voice of the people and meet their aspirations by driving the country’s development and improving the people’s well-being, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. “Therefore, the Madani government expresses its appreciation to everyone who contributed their views in the 2027 Budget Engagement Session. The 2027 Budget Engagement Session, chaired by Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, served as a prelude to the journey towards the Fifth Madani Budget, which will be tabled in Parliament on Oct 9, 2026.

items.title: FGV names Nurul Muhaniza group MD, first woman to lead company
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: FGV Holdings Bhd has appointed Nurul Muhaniza Hanafi as its group managing director, effective today, making her the first woman to lead the company. The company said Muhaniza has been serving as chairman of its board executive committee (BEC) since March. "Appointed to the FGV board on April 1, 2024, as an independent non-executive director, Muhaniza served as chairman of the board governance & risk management committee and as a member of the board nomination and remuneration committee and board audit committee," FGV said in a statement.

items.title: Vivy Yusof, husband face CBT trial as court hears RM19.5m Khazanah transfers, director records
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The Sessions Court today was told that Khazanah Nasional Berhad (Khazanah) made two transfers totalling approximately RM19.5 million into an account belonging to local fashion company Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd in March 2018. CIMB Bank Berhad, Menara KL Sentral branch manager Lee Hui Nee, 58, said a review of Khazanah’s CIMB account statements revealed that the first transfer of RM7,848,000 was recorded on March 23, 2018, while the second transfer for RM11,742,000 was made on March 26, 2018. Both payments were made via interbank transfers from Khazanah’s CIMB account to Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd’s Public Bank account,” she said.

items.title: Kampar leads Malaysia in ageing population: 12.6pc of population aged 65 and above by 2025
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 18 — Kampar has the highest proportion of older citizens in Malaysia, with 12.6 per cent of its population aged 65 and above in 2025, according to the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN). According to The Star, LPPKN deputy chairman Juwairiya Zulkifli said the figure surpasses both the national average of 8 per cent and Perak’s overall proportion of 10.2 per cent, underscoring ageing as a major demographic challenge for the district. She said Kampar’s ageing trend stems from improved life expectancy and demographic shifts, including the migration of younger residents to urban centres such as Kuala Lumpur, Selangor and Penang for work, leaving older parents behind.

items.title: Temerloh fuel tanker crash: Driver charged with reckless driving causing deaths of mother, child
items.summary: TEMERLOH, Aug 18 — A tanker lorry driver today pleaded not guilty at the Magistrate’s Court here to two counts of reckless driving that caused the deaths of a mother and her son at KM9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang here last Friday. He was charged with driving the tanker dangerously, causing the deaths of Nur Fatima Syuhada Abdullah, 39, and Muhamad Fattah Aisy Nuafal Saifulnizam, 12, at about 4pm on Aug 14. Last Friday, Nur Fatima Syuhada and Muhamad Fattah Aisy Nuafal were found burnt to death inside a car that caught fire after being crushed by a tanker lorry carrying 32,000 litres of fuel.

items.title: Woman, security guard held after Malaysian, Johor flags flown upside down
items.summary: KULAI: Police have arrested a Malaysian woman and a Nepali security guard after the Malaysian and Johor flags were flown upside down at a factory in the Indahpura industrial area. Kulai police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee said the two, aged 34 and 48, were picked up yesterday morning after pictures of the inverted flags went viral on social media. Both suspects have been remanded for four days until Aug 21 to assist in investigations under Section 5 of the Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act, Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act.

items.title: MGA targets RM100mil turnover at inaugural Malaysia Gold Festival 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Gold Association (MGA) is targeting RM100 million in turnover from the three-day Malaysia Gold Festival (MGF) 2026, scheduled to be held from Sept 18 to 20 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre (KLCC). MGA president Datuk Seri Louis Ng said the target would be driven by a combination of business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C) sales during the festival. In 2020, MGA introduced the 916 Malaysian Gold Cultural Day, which is celebrated every Sept 16 to recognise Malaysia's gold culture, promote locally crafted gold jewellery and strengthen appreciation for Malaysian craftsmanship.

items.title: Duopharma Q2 earnings jump 48pct on better product mix, stronger ringgit
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Duopharma Biotech Bhd's net profit jumped 47.8 per cent in the second quarter ended June 30, driven by higher gross profit from a more favourable product mix and a stronger ringgit. Net profit rose to RM29.86 million from RM20.20 million a year earlier, while revenue increased 5.6 per cent to RM234.35 million from RM221.78 million, according to its Bursa Malaysia filing. For the first half of the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, net profit rose 32.1 per cent to RM60.58 million from RM45.84 million.

items.title: German apartment building permits rise 14pct in June as sector recovers
items.summary: FRANKFURT: Permits to build apartments in Germany rose nearly 14 per cent in June from a year earlier, statistics office data showed on Tuesday, as the nation's property industry shows further signs of recovery. Germany's property sector entered a severe slump in 2022 at the start of the war in Ukraine Permits, which have been increasing in recent months, are an important indicator of future construction activity In June, approved permits for apartments totaled 21,600 units, up 2,600 from a year earlier "To be sure, we are coming from a low level and still are far from where we need to be in Germany," said Verena Hubertz, Germany's minister for housing Higher interest rates and inflation fears in the wake of unrest in the Middle East have recently dimmed the outlook for the German real estate industry © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: US home builder sentiment ticks up in August but remains weak overall
items.summary: NEW YORK: US home builder sentiment unexpectedly ticked higher in August, but residential construction firms' confidence remains weak overall, weighed down by economic uncertainty, high mortgage rates and steep building costs aggravated by the US-led war with Iran, a survey showed on Monday. The National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market index rose one point to a reading of 35 this month from July's unrevised level of 34. "While builder sentiment edged higher in August, builders continue to contend with high construction costs and broader economic uncertainty," NAHB Chairman Bill Owens, a home builder and remodeler from Worthington, Ohio, said in a statement.

items.title: Asking prices for UK homes show biggest August fall in eight years
items.summary: LONDON: Asking prices for newly listed homes in Britain recorded their biggest August fall since 2018 despite a modest pickup in activity after Prime Minister Andy Burnham took office, property website Rightmove said on Monday. Average asking prices fell 2.0 per cent in four weeks to August 8, sharper than the 10-year average fall of 1.3 per cent Summer slowdown and 12-year high number of homes for sale weigh on prices Asking prices were 1.0 per cent lower than a year earlier, the biggest annual fall since December 2023 London saw the sharpest fall with asking prices down 3.1 per cent annually but prices rise in the north of England Buyer demand up 5.0 per cent since Burnham became prime minister on July 20 but was 10 per cent lower than a year earlier The average two-year fixed mortgage rate rose to 5.09 per cent from 4.92 per cent a month earlier. Rightmove cut its forecast for price growth of 2.0 per cent in 2026 and to flat or a fall of up to 2y.0 per cent with risks seen from geopolitical uncertainty, higher mortgage rates and October's budget The survey was based on prices of properties put up for sale between July 12 and August 8.

items.title: Kuala Lumpur luxury home deals send average prices up 52pct: Juwai IQI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A surge in high-value subsale transactions in Kuala Lumpur has pushed the city's average house price up 52 per cent to RM1.203 million, highlighting growing activity in the luxury segment despite the market remaining largely driven by affordable and mid-market homes. Juwai IQI co-founder and group chief executive officer Kashif Ansari said properties priced between RM750,001 and RM1 million accounted for six per cent of total subsale transactions in the first half of 2026, while homes priced above RM1 million made up 10 per cent. "We saw a surprising concentration of high-value subsale transactions in Kuala Lumpur this quarter.

items.title: Loke assures RTS Link travellers: Passports accepted, QR system offered as digital option
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 18 — Passengers travelling on the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link can still use their regular passports for immigration clearance, while QR codes are available as an alternative through the digital system. Transport Minister Anthony Loke said the use of QR codes was not the only clearance method available to travellers at the Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) Complex at the RTS Link Bukit Chagar. So, the QR code is an option available to travellers, but they can also use their regular passports,” he told reporters after a media visit to the RTS Link project at the RTS Link Bukit Chagar Station here today.

items.title: Prosecution appeals Zizie Izette’s acquittal in RM2.8m corruption case tied to Felcra unit trust
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The prosecution has filed a notice of appeal against the Sessions Court’s decision to acquit and discharge actress Datin Seri Zizie Izette Abdul Samad on three charges of abetting in a RM2.8 million corruption case involving a RM150 million investment in Public Mutual Berhad unit trusts, 11 years ago. Zizie Izette’s lawyer Ridha Abdah Subri confirmed the matter when contacted. Zizie Izette, 47, was freed of three amended charges under Section 28(1)(c) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.

items.title: West River secures feed-in approval for two Perak hydropower projects
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: West River Bhd's subsidiary Neutron Power Sdn Bhd has secured feed-in approval from the Sustainable Energy Development Authority Malaysia for two small hydropower projects in Perak under the 2026 feed-in tariff (FiT) system. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the projects are located within Hutan Rizab Bukit Kinta in Ulu Kinta and Hutan Rizab Bukit Tapah in Bidor. West River said the approval marked another step in its expansion into renewable energy as the group seeks to diversify its earnings through hydropower projects.

items.title: Euro zone bonds join global selloff, yields hit multi-year highs
items.summary: LONDON: Euro zone bond yields hit multi-year highs on Tuesday, joining a global fixed-income selloff, as fading hopes for a swift end to the war in Iran drove oil prices higher and fuelled inflation concerns. Bond yields move inversely with prices. France's 10-year bond yield rose to 4.0954 per cent, its highest since November 2008.

items.title: Two‑minute Genting goldsmith heist: Suspects armed with axes escape in BMW with RM1.74m haul
items.summary: Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said police received a report on the incident at 11.39am from a private security guard. He said preliminary investigations found that three male suspects wearing face masks, caps, and jackets entered the premises and took five trays of jewellery. Azry Akmar said police are continuing investigations to track down all three suspects.

items.title: Indonesia's planned commodity exchange likely to cover palm oil, nickel, coal
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's planned exchange for "mineral and strategic commodities" will likely include palm oil, nickel and coal, a presidential spokesperson said as the government makes preparations to launch the bourse on Jan 1. "Certainly it will cover the commodities that are our primary products, such as CPO (crude palm oil), nickel, and coal," he said. Indonesia has existing commodity exchanges for palm oil, tin and some other commodities.

items.title: 5.8-magnitude earthquake hits southern Sumatra
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A moderate earthquake measuring 5.8 on the Richter scale struck southern Sumatra, Indonesia, at 2.02pm today. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a Facebook post, said the earthquake was centred at 0.8 degrees south and 98.3 degrees east, at a depth of 44km. However, MetMalaysia said there was no tsunami threat to Malaysia.

items.title: Malaysia's jewellery trade hits RM12.13bil in 1H 2026 – Matrade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's total jewellery trade grew 10 per cent to RM12.13 billion in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), sustaining the industry's strong momentum following a record performance last year. Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) deputy chief executive officer (Export Acceleration) S. Jai Shankar said the continued growth reflected the strength of the country's jewellery industry and growing global confidence in Malaysia's trade capabilities. "In 2025, Malaysia's total jewellery trade surged 22.5 per cent to an unprecedented RM22.46 billion, driven by strong growth across both exports and imports," he said in his speech at the launch of the inaugural Malaysia Gold Festival (MGF) 2026 here, today.

items.title: Penang Customs seizes RM2.53mil in cigarettes, liquor in three raids
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Penang Customs seized more than one million cigarettes and 18,400 litres of liquor worth RM2.53 million in three raids in Kedah and Penang, and arrested one man. The seizures were made in Kulim, Kedah, and Bukit Mertajam and Sungai Jawi in Penang between July 10 and July 31. Hasbollah said the first raid, conducted at 2pm on July 10, involved a house in Kulim, Kedah, where officers found 205,880 cigarette sticks and 12,464.20 litres of beer and liquor.

items.title: Elderly man jailed 13 years for killing friend in care home fight
items.summary: Judge Zamri Bakar imposed the sentence on Mansur for causing the death of Asri Asmadi, 55, at the care home in Kampung Chokru, Batu 7, Simpang Renggam, Kluang, at 7.05pm on Oct 10, 2019. The court heard that police received a call at 8.12pm that a man had died at the care home and subsequently detained Mansur for questioning. During questioning, Mansur admitted using a parang and scissors during the fight with Asri.

items.title: Boost rolls out digital banking, payments platform for SMEs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Axiata Group Bhd's majority-owned Boost Holdings Sdn Bhd has launched Boost SME, a digital platform combining business banking, payments and financing services for small and medium enterprises (SMEs). The platform allows businesses to open accounts digitally in five minutes, accept payments via DuitNow QR, online payments and cards, and receive same-day DuitNow QR settlements. Boost group chief executive officer Sheyantha Abeykoon said the platform was developed to make banking, payments and financing more accessible to businesses.

items.title: More Trump-Kim 'love'? What we know about North Korea
items.summary: US President Donald Trump says Kim Jong Un had responded to his recent overtures and praised his relationship with the North Korean leader a day after scaling back military drills with South Korea. Analysts say Kim now enjoys greater global stature, buoyed by crucial backing from Russia and China as well as an improving economy. AFP looks at what we know about the nuclear-armed country's current state: Ties with Russia North Korea has been playing a more active role in international conflict, notably backing Russia in its invasion of Ukraine.

items.title: Home Ministry uses drones to track drug addicts
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The National Anti-Drugs Agency (AADK) has deployed 18 drones to track suspected drug addicts across mapped hotspots, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today. He said the drones provide round-the-clock surveillance to ensure accurate intelligence before enforcement operations are carried out. " He said that the 18 drones enhance AADK's operational capabilities alongside its existing mapping of drug hotspots, which is conducted together with the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department.

items.title: Gobind pushes PM on equal MP allocations, calls for legislation to lock in fairness
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — DAP today reiterated its call for the government to honour Pakatan Harapan’s election pledge of equal Constituency Development Funds (CDF) for all Members of Parliament. Gobind welcomed the Prime Minister’s recent announcement of additional direct funds for constituencies but said the move did not resolve the core issue. “I therefore urge the Prime Minister to address the delay and move forward with first providing all MPs with equal allocations, and subsequently enacting legislation that permanently secures equal constituency allocations for every MP in Malaysia,” he said.

items.title: Mother fined RM6,000 for using disabled child's account in rental scam
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: A mother of five was fined RM6,000 by the Sessions court today for using her disabled child's bank account to facilitate a RM1,500 rental scam. Hafizah fined her RM6,000, in default three months' jail According to the charge, Noor Fazira used her child's bank account to facilitate a transaction that caused the victim, Anis Amera Zaini, to suffer RM1,500 in losses. The offence was committed at Jalan Anggerik 2/12, Taman Anggerik Tenggara, Bandar Tenggara, between April 30 and May 22.

items.title: Malakoff appoints related party MMC Engineering for RM26.85mil project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malakoff Corp Bhd's unit Alam Flora Environmental Solutions Sdn Bhd has appointed MMC Engineering Sdn Bhd for RM26.85 million worth of construction works for its Sustainable Facility and Eco-Park Centre in Kemaman, Terengganu. MMC Engineering is a subsidiary of MMC Corp Bhd, a major shareholder of Malakoff, making the appointment a related party transaction under Bursa Malaysia's Main Market listing requirements. Malakoff said Datuk Mohd Nazrul Izam Mansor, who represents MMC on the boards of Malakoff and Alam Flora Sdn Bhd and is also MMC group chief executive officer, is deemed interested in the contract.

items.title: Elderly far more at risk from rising heat than thought: Study
items.summary: PARIS: The threat that rising temperatures fuelled by climate change pose to the health of older people has been dramatically underestimated, according to a US modelling study published Tuesday. The research was released during a blistering northern hemisphere summer when extreme heat broke numerous records and contributed to the deaths of tens of thousands of people. For the study, a US team led by researchers at Stanford University sought to estimate how often human-caused global warming will push temperatures to levels that elderly people cannot tolerate.

items.title: Hat Yai police deny harassing Malaysian bikers over traffic offences
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Hat Yai police have denied harassing or intimidating a group of Malaysian motorcyclists, saying the enforcement action was carried out in accordance with Thai traffic laws. The clarification came after a Malaysian social media user, known as "Tok Singa", posted a video claiming that his group of 17 Malaysian bikers had been detained by Hat Yai traffic police and issued 15 summonses involving fines totalling 15,000 baht (about RM1,850). Hat Yai Traffic Police chief Police Lieutenant Colonel Weerasak Phunsak said the actual circumstances differed from those portrayed in the viral video.

items.title: Cabinet to decide policies for tighter border controls, says MCBA chief
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) will strengthen and better coordinate controls at the country's entry points while ensuring public movement is not unduly hampered. Its director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said policy and operational matters relating to MCBA's role would be left to the Cabinet to decide as part of efforts to strengthen border security. He said the priority was to manage the movement of people efficiently without compromising national security.

items.title: Malaysia and Singapore to announce RTS Link fare soon, Loke says talks moving smoothly
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 18 — An official announcement on the fare for the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link service will be made jointly by the Transport Ministries (MOT) of both countries in the near future. He said this when asked whether the RTS Link fare had been finalised. Loke said RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) was now at the final stage of discussions with the Malaysian and Singaporean governments to finalise the fare and payment mechanism for the RTS Link.

items.title: SPM 2026 written exams set November 23 to December 17, oral and practical earlier
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — The 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) written examination will be held from November 23 to December 17, the Ministry of Education (MOE) said today. In a statement today, the ministry said the Bahasa Melayu Oral Test and English Language Oral Test will be held from October 26 to 29 and November 2 to 5, respectively. The Science Practical Test will take place from November 16 to 18, followed by the Bahasa Melayu Listening Test on November 30 and the English Language Listening Test on December 1.

items.title: Transport Ministry greenlights RM60m bridge, giving Komuter passengers direct access to RTS station
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 18 — The government will build a bridge between the Bukit Chagar RTS Link Station and KTMB Komuter service to strengthen public transport integration and facilitate passenger access to the transit system. We want to encourage RTS Link users to take public transport to reach Bukit Chagar or to exit from Bukit Chagar,” he told reporters after a visit to the RTS Link project at Bukit Chagar here today. He said the Bukit Chagar RTS Link Station will also be integrated with JB Sentral, e-hailing services and other public transport, making it a multi-modal public transport hub.

items.title: Anwar resists GST comeback, eyes selective levy fixes to reinforce SST ahead of Budget 2027
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today again indicated his hesitation to reintroduce the Goods and Services Tax during a dialogue with businesses and ministries ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027, slated for October. But Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, suggested that he is open to incorporating some “elements” of the consumption levy, if it helps improve the Sales and Services Tax. GST is a ‘broad-based tax’, we tax all the people, and I disagree with that.”

items.title: Public Works Ministry spends entire RM2b road maintenance allocation, to seek more funds
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Aug 18 — The Works Ministry has fully used its roughly RM2 billion allocation for road maintenance and aims to seek more allocation, Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said today. “Hopefully, road maintenance allocations can be increased,” he said. “Road maintenance accounts for only 13 per cent,” he said.

items.title: Ahmad Maslan: Umno’s state election moves are strategy, not ‘backstabbing’ of Unity Government partners
items.summary: He said Umno and Pakatan Harapan (PH) did not have state-level agreements in Johor, Negeri Sembilan and Melaka, unlike in Penang, where he said there was an agreement. he said. he said.

items.title: Home minister: Drone surveillance boosts AADK drug enforcement, identifies 23,317 suspects
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — The National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) has identified 23,317 suspected drug addicts through surveillance by its fleet of 18 drones, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said today. He said the drones had enhanced AADK’s enforcement capabilities by allowing the agency to monitor drug hotspots around the clock, including through night flights. Saifuddin said information gathered through drone surveillance was channelled to AADK’s operations room, where it was analysed and used to guide enforcement action.

items.title: Fahmi: Facebook commits ‘most sins’ against Malaysians with online gambling, scams
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil today took a swipe at Facebook, describing the platform as the “most guilty” among social media platforms when it comes to enabling online gambling and scams in Malaysia. Fahmi said Facebook accounted for 78 per cent of online gambling content identified by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for removal between January 1 and August 17 this year. Fahmi said MCMC had sought the removal of 470,593 pieces of harmful content between January 1 and August 17, with platforms complying with 93 per cent of the requests, involving 436,661 pieces of content.

items.title: Former Chief Justice Richard Malanjum returns to practice as advocate and solicitor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Former Chief Justice Tun Richard Malanjum has been officially admitted and enrolled as an advocate and solicitor of the High Court of Malaya. Malanjum, 73, holds a historic place in the Malaysian judiciary as the first judge from Borneo to serve as Chief Justice. Malanjum possesses both these traits,” Kow said.

items.title: Malaysia's economy beats expectations with 5.7pc growth, says finance minister II
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — Malaysia’s impressive economic growth in the first half of the year, which exceeded Bank Negara Malaysia’s 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) projection of four to five per cent, demonstrates the resilience of the country’s economy. Finance Minister II, Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan, said GDP grew at a rate of 5.4 per cent in the first quarter of this year and six per cent in the second quarter, resulting in an overall economic growth of 5.7 per cent in the first half of 2026. “In fact, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) also raised Malaysia’s GDP forecast from 4.3 per cent in January 2026 to 4.7 per cent in April 2026.

items.title: Poor management, financial weakness behind 75pc of delayed projects, says Ahmad Maslan
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Aug 18 — An estimated 75 per cent of delayed and sick construction projects nationwide are due to weak management, poor operational oversight and financial shortfalls, said Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan today. He said technical issues at project sites made up the remaining 25 per cent which showed the need for contractors to strengthen their financial position, internal management and ability to deliver projects. He said CIDB records showed that Bumiputera contractors made up 47,064, or 72 per cent, of the 65,446 Grade G1 contractors registered nationwide.

items.title: Home minister: Malaysia’s entry points to get security boost after drug scandal
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 18 — A comprehensive plan to enhance security at the country’s entry points will be presented to the Cabinet tomorrow, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. He said the plan would be jointly presented with Transport Minister Anthony Loke at the meeting. The plan was prepared within two weeks following a Cabinet directive to strengthen controls at the country’s entry points through the coordination of various relevant agencies.

items.title: RTS Link aims to fast track immigration clearance in a matter of seconds
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 18 — The Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link service is expected to take only several seconds to complete a passenger’s immigration procedure once it isfully operational by early next year. Mass Rapid Transit Corporation’s (MRT Corp) RTS Link project director Zulkifli Mohamed said passengers do not need to queue long for these procedures as there are 100 e-gate lanes at the Bukit Chagar Integrated Immigration, Customs and Quarantine (ICQ) Complex. The four-kilometre RTS Link will connect Bukit Chagar station in Johor Bahru to Woodlands North station in Singapore.

items.title: Finance Ministry says e-invoices, though unpopular, are necessary to rein in shadow economy
items.summary: Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan pointed to e-invoicing among others, a policy that he said is crucial to shrink the size of the country’s massive shadow economy but was met some grumbling from mostly small enterprises. “The effort to restructure the economy is not an easy task. The size of Malaysia’s shadow economy, also referred to as the underground or informal economy, is estimated to be roughly 21 per cent to over 30 per cent of gross domestic product, depending on the estimation methodology and reporting period.

items.title: RM23,000 cash prizes up for grabs in Malaysia Day competitions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Total cash prizes of RM23,000 are among the main attractions of a series of competitions held in conjunction with the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) celebrations, in an effort to further foster patriotism among Malaysians. Communications Ministry Strategic and Corporate Communications Division assistant secretary Muhammad Khairul Nazmi Jamsari said the initiative comprises two main categories, namely the Lensa Malaysia Photojournalism Competition and the AiMAGINASI Malaysia Competition. Under the theme ‘Malaysia Madani: Kesejahteraan Dinikmati’, this year’s National Day celebrations will be held in Putrajaya, while Malaysia Day celebrations are scheduled to take place in Sarawak.

items.title: Abolition of Auku will foster critical thinking in universities, says G25 civil society group
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — The proposed abolition of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) would foster a culture of independent and critical thinking within the country’s higher learning institutions, says civil society organisation G25 Malaysia. The group of prominent retired civil servants welcomed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s assurance that any replacement law would not restrict the rights and freedoms of university students, noting that youth empowerment had to begin in higher education. It said the legislation also needed to include proper disclosure of appointments and qualifications, safeguards against political patronage and conflicts of interest, and clear standards governing the responsibilities and independence of boards.

items.title: Get ready, students: 2026 SPM schedule to be announced today
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 18 —The 2026 Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination schedule is expected to be announced this evening after receiving the approval of Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek, said Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad. He said the proposed improvement to the examination schedule would be presented by the deputy director of the Examination Syndicate to Fadhlina today for consideration and approval. He said the preparation of the new schedule took into account the views of various parties, including concerns regarding the status of several examination papers which were previously often scheduled at the end of the examination period.

items.title: Fahmi urges Malaysians to embrace ‘Aku Berjanji’, strengthen spirit of patriotism
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has urged all Malaysians to listen to and embrace the National Day and Malaysia Day (HKHM) 2026 theme song titled “Aku Berjanji”. In a post on his official Facebook page yesterday, Fahmi said the song, composed and performed by renowned singer Faizal Tahir, could further strengthen the spirit of love for the country. Earlier, Fahmi received a visit from Faizal in Putrajaya, during which the singer also shared updates on his upcoming concert, scheduled for Oct 3 at Unifi Arena, Bukit Jalil.

items.title: Firefighters battle hill forest blaze near Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah mosque
items.summary: “Fire tenders from the Shah Alam Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) arriving at the location found about seven acres (2.8 hectares) of hilly forest on fire. He said 10 officers and personnel were involved, using fire beaters and water pumps to fight the fire. “Firefighters are extinguishing remaining hot spots using water sourced from the Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) fire hydrant, supported by a water tanker, alongside creating fire breaks to prevent the fire from spreading,” he said.

items.title: ‘Change must come from the top’: Ex-deputy IGP says it is up to leaders to combat corruption
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 18 — Efforts to combat corruption and strengthen integrity comprehensively require strong political will beginning from the highest level of leadership, says former deputy inspector-general of police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay. He said top leadership must lead by example and demonstrate firm resolve, as any form of organisational transformation would only succeed if those at the top sent a clear signal of having zero tolerance for misconduct. “Change must come from the top.
